title: Wales 2-3 Portugal: Forbs snatches winner to secure top spot
subtitle: Portugal may be without Cristiano Ronaldo, but Carlos Forbs – wearing number seven – got his first international goal to secure the win.
paragraphs: Carlos Forbs came off the bench to earn 10-man Portugal a 3-2 victory over Wales, securing top spot in Nations League Group A4 in the process.
A topsy-turvy first half saw both teams take the lead, with David Brooks cancelling out Bruno Fernandes' opener before Pedro Neto levelled after Sorba Thomas had put Wales in front.
But Forbs pounced on a defensive mistake from the hosts, and though Neto was sent off for two bookable offences late on, Portugal sealed all three points in Cardiff.

Wales created their own problems in the 11th minute as Josh Sheehan was dispossessed just outside his own box by Joao Neves. He quickly spun to play in Fernandes, who swept in from the edge of the box.
Two minutes later, the hosts were back level. Harry Wilson's tight-angled effort was smothered by Diogo Costa, but Rubin Colwill recycled it to Brooks, who slotted in.
Wales took the lead in the 40th minute when Thomas drove into Portugal's box from the halfway line and kept his composure to curl a low finish past Costa.
However, their advantage only lasted three minutes as Neto peeled away at the back post to meet Trincao's looping left-sided cross.
Wilson was denied by Costa on the stroke of half-time, and Portugal dominated after the break, with Neto hitting the foot of the far post after a slaloming run down the right wing.

Portugal regained the lead in the 70th minute, with Fernandes' long pass misjudged by Ben Cabango, who nodded it out to the right where Forbs raced onto it. The new Portugal number seven cut inside and picked out the far-bottom corner to net his first international goal.

The visitors had to endure a nervy final 16 minutes, though, after Neto was sent off for two bookings in the space of 127 seconds. He kicked out at the back of Sheehan before needlessly flying into a late tackle on Brennan Johnson, but Wales failed to make their numerical advantage count.
Portugal wobble but get the job done
The post-Cristiano Ronaldo era started on a disheartening note with their 4-1 loss to Denmark, but Portugal got back to winning ways, though they were made to work hard for all three points.

Portugal have not lost back-to-back matches since September/October 2014 (v Albania and France), and they ensured that run continued against a Wales side already set to play in the League A/B play-offs.

They had 11 shots, with six of those on target as they accumulated 1.53 expected goals (xG), though Wales will feel they should have walked away with at least a point after peppering 22 attempts worth 1.76 xG on Portugal's goal (eight on target).
Fernandes got the scoring started with his first international goal since June (v Chile), ending a run of 10 straight matches without finding the back of the net for his country.

Brooks was the danger-man for Wales in the first half, though, after scoring in consecutive Wales games for the first time. It was also only the second time he has both scored and assisted in the same match for his country (also against Finland in March 2024).

Portugal have now received as many red cards under Jorge Jesus (two in six matches) as they managed in their previous 60 combined, but they managed to hold out against Wales' late press to get their hands on top spot.
There are still issues for Jesus to fix, with Portugal failing to keep a clean sheet in each of their last five matches, and he will be focused on doing so before the quarter-finals.
